subject: Physics
title: Waves, light & sound
sub: General wave properties, reflection and refraction, lenses and dispersion, the electromagnetic spectrum, sound
strategyIntro: In Co-ordinated Sciences, physics is one third of every paper: a multiple-choice paper, a structured theory paper and a paper on experiments. Your school test may be shorter, but it will be marked the same way.

strategy.title: Multiple choice
points: About a minute per question. Calculation questions: work it out on paper before you look at the options.
Wrong options are often the answer from using the formula the wrong way round (e.g. dividing instead of multiplying). Check units.
Never leave one blank. A wrong answer loses nothing.

strategy.title: Calculations
points: Three steps for full marks: write the formula, substitute the numbers, give the answer with its unit.
Convert units first: g to kg, cm to m, minutes to seconds, kW to W.
Keep the answer to 2 or 3 significant figures, like the data in the question.

strategy.title: Structured questions
points: The marks in brackets tell you how many separate points to make.
Use the keyword the syllabus uses (“resultant force”, “principal focus”), not an everyday word.
For “explain”, link cause to effect with “so” or “because”.

strategy.title: Questions on experiments
points: Name the instrument and say what you measure with it.
Repeat readings and take an average; time many oscillations or measure many sheets, then divide.
Tables: units in the column headings. Graphs: labelled axes with units, even scale, small crosses, best-fit line.

strategy.title: Easy marks people lose
points: Measuring angles of incidence and refraction from the surface instead of from the normal.
Saying refraction happens because light “changes direction”. The cause is the change in speed.
Forgetting to halve the time (or distance) in echo calculations: the sound goes there and back.
Calling sound transverse. Sound is longitudinal; light and all electromagnetic waves are transverse.

commandWords: Give a short fact or name. No explanation needed.
Give the exact meaning, ideally with the equation in words.
Say what happens or what you see, step by step.
Say why or how. Use “because” and link cause to effect.
Formula, substitution, answer with unit. Show working.
Apply what you know to a new situation. Any sensible physics scores.
A simple drawn graph or diagram showing the right shape, with labelled axes.
quizIntro: Answer in multiple-choice-paper style: about a minute each. For calculations, work out the answer first, then find it. Read the explanation after every answer.
flashIntro: Say the definition or equation out loud before you tap, then check you used the exact keywords and the right unit.

flashcards.back: Energy, without transferring matter.
Vibrations are perpendicular (at right angles) to the direction the wave travels. e.g. light and all electromagnetic waves, water ripples.
Vibrations are parallel to the direction the wave travels. e.g. sound.
The maximum displacement of a point on the wave from its rest (undisturbed) position.
Distance between a point on one wave and the same point on the next, e.g. crest to crest. Unit m.
The number of waves passing a point per second. Unit hertz (Hz).
v = fλ. Wave speed (m/s) = frequency (Hz) × wavelength (m).
A line joining points on a wave that are in step, e.g. along one crest.
Reflection off a straight barrier; refraction where depth changes (waves slow in shallow water and wavelength shortens); diffraction (spreading) through a gap or round an edge.
Spreading is greatest when the gap is about the same size as the wavelength. A gap much wider than the wavelength gives little diffraction.
A line drawn at 90° to a surface where a ray meets it. All angles are measured from the normal.
Angle of incidence = angle of reflection.
Same size as the object; as far behind the mirror as the object is in front; upright; virtual; laterally inverted (left and right swapped).
The change in direction of light passing from one medium to another, caused by a change in its speed.

flashcards.front: Light entering a denser medium (air → glass)
flashcards.back: It slows down and bends towards the normal. Leaving (glass → air) it speeds up and bends away from the normal. Along the normal: no bending.
n = sin i ÷ sin r (for light going from air into the material). Glass is about 1.5.
The angle of incidence (in the denser medium) for which the angle of refraction is 90°.
All the light is reflected inside the denser medium. Happens when light goes towards a less dense medium at an angle of incidence greater than the critical angle.
Light travels along a thin glass fibre by repeated total internal reflection, even round bends. Used for communications (internet, phone) and endoscopes in medicine.
n = 1 ÷ sin c.
Thicker in the middle. Refracts parallel rays so they meet at a point (the principal focus).
The line through the centre of a lens, at right angles to the lens.
The point where rays parallel to the principal axis meet after passing through a converging lens.
Distance from the centre of the lens to the principal focus.
Ray parallel to the axis → refracts through the principal focus on the far side. Ray through the centre of the lens → carries straight on.
Formed where rays actually meet; can be shown on a screen. A converging lens gives a real, inverted image when the object is further away than F.
Formed where rays only appear to come from; cannot be shown on a screen.
Image is real, inverted, diminished (smaller), and between F and 2F on the other side (as in a camera or the eye).
Object closer to the lens than F. Image is virtual, upright, magnified and on the same side as the object.
A prism splits white light into a spectrum because each colour is refracted by a different amount. Order: red, orange, yellow, green, blue, indigo, violet. Violet is refracted most.
Light of a single frequency (one colour).
Radio, microwaves, infrared, visible, ultraviolet, X-rays, gamma rays. Wavelength gets shorter and frequency higher along this list.
Transverse; travel at the same speed in a vacuum (3.0 × 10⁸ m/s, about the same in air); transfer energy; can be reflected and refracted.
Radio and television broadcasting and communication.
Satellite television and phones, mobile phones, microwave ovens.
Electric grills and heaters, TV remote controls, intruder alarms, thermal imaging, optical fibres.
Vision, photography, illumination.
Security marking (invisible ink), detecting fake bank notes, sterilising water.
Medical imaging (seeing bones) and security scanners at airports.
Sterilising food and medical equipment; detecting and treating cancer.
Microwaves: internal heating of body cells. Infrared: skin burns. Ultraviolet: damage to surface cells and eyes, skin cancer. X-rays and gamma: mutation or damage to cells (cancer).
By vibrating sources, e.g. a guitar string, a loudspeaker cone, vocal cords.
Longitudinal. Needs a medium (solid, liquid or gas) to travel through, so cannot travel through a vacuum.
Compression: particles pushed closer together (higher pressure). Rarefaction: particles further apart (lower pressure).
About 20 Hz to 20 000 Hz (20 kHz).
Sound with a frequency above 20 kHz, too high for humans to hear.
In air about 330–350 m/s. Faster in liquids, and fastest in solids.
A reflection of sound from a hard surface.
The sound travels there and back, so distance to the surface = (speed × time) ÷ 2.

flashcards.front: Measuring the speed of sound in air
flashcards.back: Two people a measured large distance apart. One makes a sound with a visible action; the other times from seeing to hearing it. Speed = distance ÷ time; repeat and average.
Higher frequency = higher pitch. Larger amplitude = louder sound.

quiz.q: A wave has a frequency of 50 Hz and a wavelength of 0.20 m. What is its speed?
quiz.why: v = fλ = 50 × 0.20 = 10 m/s. 250 m/s comes from dividing f by λ.

quiz.q: Which of these is a longitudinal wave?
quiz.why: Sound vibrations are along the direction of travel. All electromagnetic waves and water ripples are transverse.

quiz.q: What is the amplitude of a wave?
options: Maximum displacement from the rest position
quiz.why: Amplitude is measured from the rest position to a crest, so it is half the crest-to-trough height.

quiz.q: Water waves move from deep water into shallow water. What happens?
options: Frequency decreases, speed is the same
quiz.why: Waves slow down in shallower water. Frequency stays the same, so from v = fλ the wavelength gets shorter.

quiz.q: A sound wave in air has a wavelength of 0.68 m. The speed of sound is 340 m/s. What is its frequency?
(Extended) When do waves diffract most through a gap?
options: When the gap is about the same size as the wavelength
When the gap is much wider than the wavelength
When the waves have a large amplitude
quiz.why: Diffraction is greatest when the gap width is similar to the wavelength.

quiz.q: A ray hits a plane mirror with an angle of incidence of 35°. What is the angle of reflection?
quiz.why: Angle of reflection = angle of incidence. 55° is the angle to the mirror surface, not to the normal.

quiz.q: An object is 2 m in front of a plane mirror. How far is the image from the object?
quiz.why: The image is 2 m behind the mirror, so it is 2 + 2 = 4 m from the object.

quiz.q: What happens when light passes from air into glass at an angle?
options: It slows down and bends towards the normal
It speeds up and bends towards the normal
It slows down and bends away from the normal
It speeds up and bends away from the normal
quiz.why: Glass is optically denser, so light slows down and bends towards the normal.

quiz.q: When does total internal reflection happen?
options: Light goes from air into glass at a large angle
The angle of incidence is less than the critical angle
Light goes from glass towards air at more than the critical angle
quiz.why: Both conditions are needed: travelling towards a less dense medium, and i greater than the critical angle.

quiz.q: Which is a use of optical fibres?
options: An endoscope to see inside the body
quiz.why: An endoscope carries light down to the organ and back by total internal reflection.

quiz.q: (Extended) A ray in air enters glass with i = 50° and r = 30°. What is the refractive index? (sin 50° = 0.77, sin 30° = 0.50)
quiz.why: n = sin i ÷ sin r = 0.77 ÷ 0.50 = 1.54 (about 1.5). 1.67 wrongly divides the angles, not their sines.

quiz.q: (Extended) Glass has a refractive index of 1.5. What is its critical angle?
White light passes through a prism. Which colour is refracted the most?
quiz.why: Violet is bent most and red least, so the spectrum runs red to violet.

quiz.q: What is meant by a real image?
options: One that can be formed on a screen
One that is the same size as the object
One that forms behind a mirror
quiz.why: Light rays actually meet at a real image, so it can be caught on a screen.

quiz.q: An object is placed three focal lengths from a converging lens. What is the image like?
quiz.why: Object beyond 2F gives a real, inverted, smaller image between F and 2F.

quiz.q: What is the focal length of a lens?
options: The distance from the centre of the lens to the principal focus
The distance from the object to the image
quiz.why: Focal length is measured from the centre of the lens to the principal focus.

quiz.q: In a ray diagram, what happens to a ray passing through the centre of a thin converging lens?
options: It passes straight through without bending
It bends towards the principal axis
It passes through the principal focus
quiz.why: A ray through the optical centre is not deviated. It is the ray parallel to the axis that goes through F.

quiz.q: (Extended) Where must an object be placed to use a converging lens as a magnifying glass?
options: Closer to the lens than F
quiz.why: Closer than F, the rays leaving the lens spread out, so they seem to come from a magnified, upright, virtual image.

quiz.q: Which electromagnetic wave has the longest wavelength?
quiz.why: Radio waves are at the long-wavelength, low-frequency end of the spectrum.

quiz.q: Which waves are used to sterilise medical equipment?
quiz.why: Gamma rays kill bacteria and can pass through sealed packaging.

quiz.q: Which region lies between visible light and X-rays?
quiz.why: The order is … infrared, visible, ultraviolet, X-rays, gamma.

quiz.q: Which waves does a TV remote control use?
quiz.why: Remote controls send short-range infrared signals.

quiz.q: A radio station broadcasts at 1.5 × 10⁶ Hz. What is the wavelength? (speed = 3.0 × 10⁸ m/s)
What do all electromagnetic waves have in common?
quiz.why: All travel at 3.0 × 10⁸ m/s in a vacuum. They are all transverse, with different wavelengths and frequencies.

quiz.q: What is a harmful effect of too much ultraviolet radiation?
quiz.why: UV damages surface cells and eyes and can cause skin cancer. Internal heating is the danger from microwaves.

quiz.q: Why can sound not travel through space?
options: There are no particles (no medium) to vibrate
quiz.why: Sound needs a medium. Space is a vacuum. Light, an electromagnetic wave, can still travel through it.

quiz.q: Which sound can a human with normal hearing hear?
quiz.why: The human range is about 20 Hz to 20 kHz. 50 kHz and 2 MHz are ultrasound; 5 Hz is too low.

quiz.q: A note is played more loudly but at the same pitch. What has changed?
quiz.why: Loudness depends on amplitude. Same pitch means the frequency is unchanged.

quiz.q: How does the speed of sound in steel compare with its speed in air?
quiz.why: Sound travels fastest in solids, then liquids, then gases.

quiz.q: A girl shouts towards a cliff and hears the echo 0.60 s later. Sound travels at 340 m/s. How far away is the cliff?
quiz.why: Distance there and back = 340 × 0.60 = 204 m, so the cliff is 204 ÷ 2 = 102 m away.

quiz.q: What is ultrasound?
quiz.why: Ultrasound has a frequency above the upper limit of human hearing, 20 kHz.

examIntro: Theory-paper style. Write your answer first, then open the mark scheme and give yourself one mark per point you made clearly. In calculations, the formula, the substitution and the answer with unit each earn marks.

exam.q: Describe the difference between a transverse wave and a longitudinal wave.
points: Transverse: vibrations are at right angles to the direction of travel (energy transfer)
Longitudinal: vibrations are parallel to the direction of travel

exam.q: A water wave has a frequency of 2.5 Hz and a wavelength of 0.40 m. Calculate its speed.
points: v = fλ

exam.q: In a ripple tank, 12 waves pass a point in 4.0 s. The distance from the first to the fifth crest is 20 cm. Calculate (a) the frequency, (b) the wavelength in m, (c) the wave speed.
points: (b) Five crests contain four wavelengths

exam.q: Describe the image formed by a plane mirror.
points: Same size as the object
Same distance behind the mirror as the object is in front
Upright
Virtual (cannot be shown on a screen)
Laterally inverted

exam.q: (Extended) Light in air hits a glass block with an angle of incidence of 40°. The refractive index of the glass is 1.5. Calculate the angle of refraction. (sin 40° = 0.64)
points: n = sin i ÷ sin r
sin r = 0.43

exam.q: Explain how light travels along a curved optical fibre, and state one use of optical fibres.
points: Light enters one end of the fibre
It hits the inside surface (glass–air or core–cladding boundary) at an angle greater than the critical angle
So it is totally internally reflected
This happens again and again along the fibre, even round bends
Very little light escapes
Use: endoscope / telephone and internet cables (communications)
exam.note: Any 4 for the explanation, plus 1 for the use.

exam.q: State what is meant by (a) the principal focus and (b) the focal length of a converging lens.
points: (a) The point where rays parallel to the principal axis meet after passing through the lens
(b) The distance from the centre of the lens to the principal focus

exam.q: Describe what happens when a narrow beam of white light passes through a glass prism.
points: The light is refracted (slows down and bends) on entering and leaving
Different colours are refracted by different amounts
White light is split into a spectrum (dispersion)
Red is refracted least, violet most

exam.q: An object 4.0 cm tall stands 15 cm from a converging lens of focal length 5.0 cm. Describe how to draw a ray diagram to find the image, and state three properties of the image.
points: Draw a ray from the top of the object parallel to the principal axis, refracting through the principal focus on the far side
Draw a ray from the top of the object through the centre of the lens, carrying straight on
The top of the image is where the two rays cross
Image is real
Image is inverted
Image is diminished (smaller than the object), between F and 2F

exam.q: State two properties that all electromagnetic waves share.
points: Transverse
Same speed in a vacuum (3.0 × 10⁸ m/s)
Transfer energy
Can travel through a vacuum
Can be reflected / refracted

exam.q: A microwave oven uses waves of frequency 2.4 × 10⁹ Hz. Calculate their wavelength. (speed = 3.0 × 10⁸ m/s)
points: λ = v ÷ f

exam.q: For X-rays and ultraviolet, state one use and one harmful effect of each.
points: X-rays use: medical imaging of bones / airport security scanners
X-rays harm: mutation or damage to cells, causing cancer
Ultraviolet use: security marking / detecting fake bank notes / sterilising water
Ultraviolet harm: damage to skin cells and eyes, skin cancer

exam.q: Explain why astronauts on the Moon cannot hear each other directly, even when close together.
points: Sound needs a medium (particles) to travel through
There is no air on the Moon (it is a vacuum)

exam.q: Describe how two students could measure the speed of sound in air on a playing field.
points: Measure a large distance between them (e.g. 200 m or more) with a tape or trundle wheel
One student makes a loud sound with a visible action (claps blocks / bangs cymbals)
The other starts a stopwatch on seeing the action and stops it on hearing the sound
Speed = distance ÷ time
Repeat several times and average

exam.q: A ship sends a sound pulse down to the sea bed. The echo returns 0.40 s later. Sound travels at 1500 m/s in water. Calculate the depth of the sea.
points: distance = speed × time
The pulse travels there and back, so halve it
Depth = 300 m
